title: Everything You Believe In Is a Lie

direction.centralDeclaration: Everything you believe in is a lie.
direction.narrator: Big Daddy / Mr. Buttons, unreliable fictional eyewitness
direction.framing: The government is depicted as a Walt-Disney-like spectacle machine; soldiers are 'worm dogs' close to the sand who carry the complicated truth absent from the broadcast.
direction.thematicQuestion: Who gets to tell a war story, and what happens to comrades when the television version conflicts with what they remember?
direction.preferredMood: 1990s triumphal TV packaging tears into exhausted trench-level testimony, then dark industrial/oni/JRPG alternate-history menace.
direction.allegationBoundary: 'Desert Storm was a lie' and 'everything you were told was a lie' are fictional, first-person claims about propaganda and memory, not documentary conclusions or claims about actual Disney government control.

bigDaddy.role: young soldier later called Big Daddy

realWorldAnchors.event: Coalition units deployed in Saudi Arabia for Desert Shield at Saudi invitation
Desert Storm coalition air campaign began
Coalition ground campaign began; rapidly concluded by February 28
Iraqi missile attacks reached Israel and Saudi Arabia

historicalFiction.terminologyBoundary: In public-history captions, Saudi Arabia was the site of coalition deployment/stationing, not the Iraqi occupation. A fictional character can subjectively describe the prolonged foreign troop presence as an 'occupation' when the viewpoint is clearly labeled. Iraq occupied Kuwait.
historicalFiction.sacredGeographyBoundary: Israel, Jerusalem and the Holy Land may enter as map, missiles and comparative Abrahamic sacred symbolism. Do not imply these places are interchangeable with Saudi bases, or equate a religious population with military decisions; distinguish beliefs from propaganda exploiting them.
historicalFiction.alternateHistoryBoundary: Anything involving secret pre-release MMORPG access in 1990-1991, Anti-Daddy founding Google, or magical warped chronology remains explicit fictional alternate history.

sceneSnapshot.cue: prelude / first atmosphere, no lyric line pinned
sceneSnapshot.scene: A lacquered 1990s television news pageant shows a clean, smiling victory story. Beneath its glossy screen, desert dust swirls and dead pixels form a worm.

sceneSnapshot.cue: first verse entrance, owner-selected first lyric pending
sceneSnapshot.scene: Desert Shield: young Big Daddy and Anti-Daddy prepare gear at a Saudi camp, heads shaved. Dog tags and Mr. Buttons callsign meet the lens. The smile on the TV does not match their faces.
sceneSnapshot.camera: eye-level two-shot drifting to close details
sceneSnapshot.purpose: introduce comrades and the propaganda/reality contrast

sceneSnapshot.cue: first intensification / verse turn, exact bar pending
sceneSnapshot.scene: News anchors call the war simple. A radio crackles. Big Daddy looks up; the camera cuts from their faces to the explosive night onset of Desert Storm.
sceneSnapshot.camera: hard match-cut from monitor white to desert night

sceneSnapshot.cue: aggressive vocal section / next verse entrance pending
sceneSnapshot.scene: Fictional frontline combat montage: armor movement, dust, flares, harsh radios, silhouettes and terrified silence. The remembered war resists the packaged victory reel.
sceneSnapshot.camera: ground-level rapid fragments, not glorifying casualties
sceneSnapshot.purpose: the worm dogs begin to testify

sceneSnapshot.scene: A nonlinear recoil from battle to prolonged stationing in Saudi Arabia: tents, heat, unanswered letters, tired soldiers, a surreal amusement-park marquee on the horizon.
sceneSnapshot.camera: slow lateral track and backward temporal dissolve
sceneSnapshot.purpose: interrogate what presence, protection and occupation mean to narrator

sceneSnapshot.scene: Period map isolates Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Iraq, Israel and Jerusalem. Missile-warning broadcast for Israel collides with imagery of holy places and competing uses of sacred language.
sceneSnapshot.camera: map/archival-style projection rather than geographically impossible one-location montage
sceneSnapshot.purpose: show the gap between sacred belief and political messaging

sceneSnapshot.scene: The televised spectacle melts into static. Big Daddy faces lens: 'Everything you believe in is a lie.' An echo shows Anti-Daddy half obscured behind the same military frame.
sceneSnapshot.camera: direct-address locked close-up with double exposure

sceneSnapshot.scene: Present-day military gear survives in a trunk, distinct from Pirate Wolverine's later stolen digital epic armor. Anti-Daddy's future long ponytail silhouette enters via a glitch. The next story is the betrayal.
sceneSnapshot.camera: match-cut metal buckle to virtual armor texture and cut black
sceneSnapshot.purpose: bridge war prologue to existing two-world lore
